newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Kohler says current trading acceptable.
newsitem.headline: Kohler says current trading acceptable.

text.p: South African packaging group Kohler Ltd said on Friday that trading since September had been acceptable in a tough and competitive market, and that it would still see real earnings growth.

"Consumer spending remains slow and this is having an impact on our packaging businesses...that said, the group's first half earnings will reflect real growth measured against an excellent first six months last year," chief executive Richard Bruyns told the firm's annual shareholders' meeting.
Bruyns said the firm was expecting a gradual reval of consumer spending as 1997 progresses.
Kohler is controlled by Malbak, which announced details of its unbundling on Thursday.
The move will leave Kohler and British packaging group MY Holdings Plc within Malbak, turning the firm from a conglomerate into a packaging concern.
